text: At the end of the twenty years during which Solomon had built the house of the LORD and his own palace,
Solomon rebuilt the towns that Huram had given him, and he settled Israelites in them.
Solomon then marched against Hamath-zobah and overpowered it.
He built Tadmor in the wilderness, along with all the storage towns he built in Hamath.
He built up Upper Beth-horon and Lower Beth-horon as fortified cities, with walls, gates, and bars,

as well as Baalath and all the storage towns that belonged to him, and all the towns for his chariots and for his cavalry—whatever he desired to build in Jerusalem, in Lebanon, and throughout the land under his rule.
As for all the people who were left of the Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, who were not Israelites—
that is, their descendants who remained in the land after them, whom the Israelites had not wiped out—Solomon conscripted them for forced labor, as they are to this day.
But Solomon made none of the Israelites slaves for his work; they were his fighting men, his officers and captains, and the commanders of his chariots and cavalry.

versions.text: But Solomon made none of the Israelites slaves for his work; they were his soldiers, the commanders of his officers, and the commanders of his chariots and cavalry.
versions.explanation: "The commanders of his officers" is opaque in English; שָׁלִישָׁיו refers to chariot officers/adjutants, so a clearer rendering such as "his officers and captains" reads better aloud without losing the sense.

text: These were King Solomon's chief officials—two hundred fifty of them—who supervised the people.

Solomon brought Pharaoh's daughter up from the City of David to the house he had built for her, for he said, "No wife of mine shall live in the house of David king of Israel, because the places the ark of the LORD has entered are holy."

versions.text: Solomon brought Pharaoh's daughter up from the City of David to the house he had built for her, for he said, "My wife shall not live in the house of David king of Israel, because the places the ark of the LORD has entered are holy."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew is indefinite ("a wife of mine"), stating a general principle rather than referring to one particular wife; "No wife of mine" is both more accurate and rhythmically stronger.

text: Then Solomon offered burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar of the LORD that he had built in front of the portico,

presenting each day's offering as Moses had commanded, for the Sabbaths, the New Moons, and the three annual festivals—the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the Festival of Weeks, and the Festival of Booths.

Following the instructions of his father David, he appointed the divisions of the priests for their service and the Levites for their duties, to offer praise and to assist the priests according to each day's requirement, and the gatekeepers by their divisions at the various gates; for this was what David, the man of God, had commanded.
They did not depart from the king's command concerning the priests and the Levites in any matter, including the treasuries.
So all of Solomon's work was carried out, from the day the foundation of the house of the LORD was laid until its completion. The house of the LORD was finished.
Then Solomon went to Ezion-geber and to Eloth on the seacoast in the land of Edom.
And Huram sent him ships with his own servants, men who knew the sea. They sailed with Solomon's servants to Ophir, took on four hundred fifty talents of gold, and brought it back to King Solomon.
